reason:
It survives the schedule lens, with four fixes. The deadline is not the binding constraint. Every GPU step is under 1.5 h of wall time, and there are about 3 days of slack for one bug-fix loop. The cited numbers check out: out_full_P.log leak5 OOF gives none 1.6861, public head 1.5254 mean and 1.3501 median um on 199 videos / 125,700 pairs, and 1.5375 on the 179 out-of-sample videos. The x138 module (decoded from experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim) makes the change a small edit: sample_features is a 7-offset integer gather, and index_features already contains the 8-corner trilinear code.

Problems found:
(1) The protocol says to exclude '10 probable x138 training videos'. The public head's probable training set is 20 stems, 10 per embryo (tools/train_coordhead.py x138_probable_train; the list is in out_full_P/report.json). The 40-video capture must avoid all 20, or the gate is partly in-sample.
(2) The existing capture saves only the 224-d features at INTEGER peaks. Pass-2 features cannot be rebuilt from those 7 samples (trilinear needs off-grid neighbours), so a new GPU capture is mandatory.
(3) The evaluation needs the GT geff. This container has none. out_full_P was produced on the user's PC (data_dir C:\Users\vital\...), so the gate verdict is a user action, not an agent step.
(4) refine() raises when |shift| > 2.00001 um measured from the integer peak. The cascade must clip the cumulative shift before this assert, or the pass-2 kernel crashes on the hidden test.

Schedule details:
- The 5070 Ti speed of 70-100 s/video is unmeasured (FRIEND_A_RUN.md step 1 still asks friend A for X).
- The idea's timeline assumes the user pushes kernels at 00:00 UTC. Realistically the capture starts on the morning of 26 Sep.
- The Kaggle 2-concurrent-session limit serialises the dummy run after the capture, unless it runs on sasyami.

Value caveat relevant to scheduling: the expected +0.001 is far below the LB noise of ~0.003. The rule 'kill if the drop is >= 0.002' is close to a coin flip, so the LB slot is mainly a crash/runtime/node-count check and the decision must rest on the offline gate.
fix_if_any:
(a) Exclude all 20 x138_probable_train stems from out_full_P/report.json. Pick 40 videos, 20 per embryo, from the other 179, preferring GT-rich stems via build_capture_kernel.gt_counts.
(b) capture2 = the existing chcap kernel plus a module-text change in the capture branch. After saving the integer-peak features, load the public head (the dataset is already attached in the exp51-derived kernel), compute the pass-1 float position with clipping, and save features_p1 = the 224-d TRILINEAR features at that position. The compaction keeps features_p1 under the same keep mask. The same capture then serves damp 0.5 and 1.0 on CPU, and gate (c) runs on the 'sampled' rows.
(c) The eval script (agent, from train_coordhead's loaders) computes the fixed pairs <= 4 um and the gates per embryo. The USER runs it on his PC with --data-dir pointing at the local train folder. Alternatively, capture2 stores each kept peak's matched GT vector, so eval needs only the npz.
(d) The cascade patch clips the total displacement to < 2 um BEFORE x138's assert, and keeps PASSES=1 byte-identical. The byte-identity is tested on synthetic tensors here, including trilinear == integer gather at integer coords.
(e) Treat the LB slot as a safety check. Adopt on gate pass + no crash + public >= #34 - 0.003. Do not read a +0.001 difference as signal.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000..+0.002 expected (about +0.001 if the gate passes; P(gate) ~0.35 is a guess, so about +0.0004 in expectation). This cannot be resolved on the LB (noise ~0.003).
realistic_private_gain: Similar, +0.000..+0.002. The mechanism has no embryo-specific parameter and the gate is per embryo. The public head's residual bias (z +0.40, y +0.29, x +0.35 um; out_full_P leak5) may be partly an annotation convention, so pass 2 could fit the train embryos' convention. Gate (c) only partly guards against this.
critical_path:
1. Agent container, 25 Sep 11:30-16:30 UTC, ~4-5 h. Write the capture2 patch in build_capture_kernel (module capture branch + features_p1 compaction), an eval-only script (fixed pairs + gates a-c per embryo, reusing train_coordhead loaders), and a probe patch on exp56 (V1284_PASSES/V1284_DAMP, cumulative clip < 2 um). Add synthetic CPU tests: PASSES=1 byte-identical, and trilinear == integer gather at integer coords. None of this can be run end to end here (no data/weights).
2. Around 17:00-20:00 UTC, #34 result: a confirmed x138 base is required for the probe to be meaningful.
3. USER, 26 Sep ~06:00-09:00 UTC (after the 00:00 reset, when awake; or 25 Sep evening on sasyami if quota and friend A's consent allow). Push 2 capture2 kernels on Kaggle vitaliineibauer T4x2, 20 videos each. At 201-214 s/video (the Kaggle pilot figure), 20 videos come to ~70 min + ~15 min setup, so ~1.2-1.5 h wall. Total ~2.5-3 GPU-h (the brief's 7.2 GPU-h/199 videos would give ~1.5 h). Friend A's 5070 Ti is optional (speed unmeasured, availability uncertain).
4. USER PC, CPU, ~0.5-1 h after the kernels finish, 26 Sep ~08:30-11:00: download the outputs, run eval with the local GT, gate verdict.
5. Kaggle, ~0.5-0.7 h GPU, 26 Sep ~10:30-12:00: dummy run of exp56 + cascade on the 4 test videos (exp51 took 1,713 s). This is gate (d): node/edge counts within 1% of exp56 plus a valid CSV. It must follow step 3 on vitalii (2-session cap) or run in parallel on sasyami.
6. USER submit, 26 Sep ~12:00-14:00 UTC. x138-type scoring takes 7-10 h, so the score arrives ~26 Sep 20:00-24:00 UTC.

Slack to the 29 Sep 10:00 cutoff is ~2.5 days: enough for one full capture bug-fix loop (+1 day) and slot contention with other ideas. The extra head pass is negligible against the 12 h limit.

P(scored by the cutoff | gate passes and the team runs it) ~0.85. If the gate fails (P ~0.65), no slot is spent; that is a correct kill, not a schedule failure.
